findings.evidence: carried R2-B1/R2-E2/R3-B3/R4-B3: same synchronous provider cancellation callback stall after timeout in unchanged external recovery code. Preserve verdict/route, skip reverification, no duplicate entry.

ValidateFields checks time before awaiting GetKeyRingAsync, with no later time check before ValidateAsync returns to the actor state barrier. A valid signed request can expire during that await and still read/mutate actor state. Reuse expiry/field validation after asynchronous authentication and prove exact-expiry rejection with suspended key retrieval before any state access.

ListCandidatesAsync returns its persisted Candidates list without filtering or rejecting null elements. The indexed scan orders nulls first, charges each to the finite slice and advances indexedAfter only for non-null elements. A full slice of nulls is repeated every pass and healthy later candidates starve. This unchanged external reminder boundary needs bounded malformed-entry progress.
carried R3-B5/R4-B5: same invalid candidate ActorId persisted as indexed cursor despite validation failure in unchanged external code. Preserve verdict/route, skip reverification, no duplicate entry.

Distinct immutable Ordinal roles form different effect identities, but CreateWitness uses the unchanged schedule tuple without ordinal. Same tenant/item/kind/due/revision roles therefore share a reminder name and SameWitness rejects their ordinal difference as collision, preventing independent arming. The new multiple-role test changes both due and revision and misses this case. This external feature needs an owner decision on compatible role scheduling or an explicit validated restriction; do not change the frozen identity codec in Story 6.4.

ClaimDiscoveryAsync CAS-replaces owner/generation immediately even for an unfinished active owner; UpdateDiscoveryAsync rejects that old owner. Two healthy replicas can interleave fresh claims around slower convergence and invalidate each other before cursor writes, repeating the previous slice. External reminder discovery needs an interleaved replica test and bounded ownership/progress semantics.
carried R2-B6/R3-B7/R4-B7: same missing translator-visible fields in the unchanged retained process digest. Preserve verdict/route, skip reverification, no duplicate entry.

The claim treats the command budget as a serialized control-record guarantee. EventStoreProcessOptions explicitly documents MaxCommandBytesPerEnvelope/Page as maximum copied command bytes; runner admission and persisted validation count those payload/type bytes consistently. JSON/Base64 structural overhead exceeding that copied-byte value does not violate the stated contract. A separate serialized ceiling would be a new requirement rather than this demonstrated budget defect.

ReadProof deserializes missing v to the property initializer Version=1; new owner/applied-proof readers then accept that default and only require nonblank terminal time. The approved completion contract says missing evidence is unproven, never defaults. Require an explicit supported receipt version and valid UTC terminal time for Completed proof, preserving prepared/recovery marker shapes, writer bytes and guard-off legacy parsing.

ApplyPersistedLifecycle preserves producer metadata for stable Idle, and StampProjectionBacked keeps Degraded. The new guard branch then overwrites it with Current or Unknown while IsDegraded remains true. Current also passes the public CanMutate lifecycle policy, so a degraded view can become mutation-confirmed. Preserve Degraded and derive compatibility fields through the existing policy; test proven and unresolved guard outcomes.

Verified additional cancellation trigger for the existing callback-isolation defect: the worker token is linked directly to caller cancellation, so a blocking provider callback runs synchronously on caller.Cancel as well as the timeout catch. The isolated unchanged-source reproduction leaves both caller cancellation and RunConvergenceAsync pending until its callback gate opens. Group with D1 rather than append a second deferred root cause; include host-shutdown impact in that pending entry.
